Title: 12 Logistics Words Every Dispatcher Needs: A1 Business English Vocabulary
Description: Send, receive, load, unload, deliver, in stock, gate, production line. Twelve logistics words with simple meanings for adult beginners who work with trucks, parts and warehouses. Teach them on a small board of trucks and pallets so students have something true to talk about. Save it for your business English students. From Dispatch Desk, an A1 series for logistics.

Title: Classroom Mistake #1: “Yesterday I Had Gone” — When Not to Use the Past Perfect
Description: Once students learn the past perfect, they attach had to everything. The rule: past perfect needs a second point in the past to look back from. No anchor, no had. The fix, the reason and a one-line drill. Part of a series of real classroom mistakes. Save it for your B1 class. From Planet Earth, You Are a Crew (B1–B2).
Keywords: past perfect mistakes, common esl mistakes, b1 grammar, past perfect vs past simple, grammar tips

Title: Classroom Mistake #2: “I Was Used to Play” — Used To vs Be Used To
Description: I was used to play football → I used to play football. Used to + base form for a finished habit, no was. And they are used to doing it when you mean familiar with. The fix, the reason and the question to ask every time: habit or one moment? Save it for your B2 class. From The Overlooked Story of America.
Keywords: used to vs be used to, common esl mistakes, b2 grammar, past habits, grammar tips

Title: Is, Are, Am or Do? One Question Decides the First Word (A1 ESL)
Description: Is there an action word? No: Is / Are / Am (Is Marek here?). Yes: Do (Do you work here?). A one-page rule with short answers and the mistake every beginner makes: Are you work here? Save it for your A1 students. From Dispatch Desk, an A1 business English series for logistics.
Keywords: be or do, a1 grammar, esl questions, verb be, beginner esl

Title: Classroom Mistake #3: “Does She Works?” — Where the -s Goes
Description: Does she works here? → Does she work here? The -s comes once: in a question or negative it moves to does. Plus she doesn't like coffee and he gets up at 5 a.m. The fix, the reason and a game that makes students ask Does he…? fifty times. Save it for your beginners. From Who Is Mr. Fox? (A1–A2).
Keywords: present simple mistakes, does she, a1 grammar, common esl mistakes, third person s

Title: Classroom Mistake #4: “On Christmas” — At, On and In with Time
Description: See you on Christmas → See you at Christmas. Holidays take at, days take on, months and years take in. A one-glance table (at Easter, on Friday, in November) plus a quick drill. Save it before the holidays. From Traditions and Customs (B1).
Keywords: prepositions of time, at on in, common esl mistakes, a2 grammar, christmas esl

Title: Classroom Mistake #5: “Yes, He's.” — Short Answers Need the Full Word
Description: Is Tom here? Yes, he's. → Yes, he is. After yes, always the full word; the short form is only for no (No, he isn't). Two more examples and the boomerang rule to fix it. Save it for your A2 class. From the Short Answers lesson (A2–B1).
Keywords: short answers mistakes, yes he is, a2 grammar, common esl mistakes, contractions

Title: The Late Truck: A Ready A1 Business English Phone Role Play
Description: Hello, this is … . The truck is late. What time does it arrive? Which gate does the driver use? A ready A1 phone role play where the student gets two facts and writes a three-sentence plan, plus the two question mistakes to watch for. Save it for your adult beginners at work. From Dispatch Desk (A1 logistics).
Keywords: business english role play, phone english, a1 speaking, logistics english, question words

Title: Classroom Mistake #6: “Did She Walked?” — The Verb After Did
Description: Did she walked to work? → Did she walk to work? After did and didn't, the verb goes back to the base form, because English moves the past to did. Plus she didn't go home. The fix, the reason and a signal-word drill. Save it for your A2 class. From Past Present Future Worksheets (A2–B1).
Keywords: past simple mistakes, did questions, a2 grammar, common esl mistakes, base form

Title: She Drives. Does She Drive? The Whole Present Simple on One Table
Description: Positive, negative, question for I / you / we / they and he / she / it, the spelling of -es and has, and the rule that the -s comes once. Plus a classic beginner puzzle: The service is open vs The service opens at 7:00. Save it for your A1 students. From Dispatch Desk (A1 logistics).
Keywords: present simple chart, a1 grammar, does doesnt, esl grammar cheat sheet, he she it

Title: Classroom Mistake #7: “You Must Change This” — Feedback That Sounds Like an Order
Description: You must change this → I'd suggest changing this. In feedback, must sounds like an order; I'd suggest, you could try and what if you…? turn it into an invitation. Two more rewrites and a quick role play to make students hear the difference. Save it for your adult learners. From Giving Feedback (A2–B2).
Keywords: polite english, giving feedback, business english, common esl mistakes, soft language

Title: Classroom Mistake #8: “I Amn't Late” — Negatives with Be
Description: I amn't late → I'm not late. Amn't doesn't exist: I'm not, he isn't, they aren't. Plus two more beginner traps: Is in the office (She's in the office) and Yes, I'm (Yes, I do). Save it for your A1 students. From Dispatch Desk, an A1 business English series.
Keywords: verb be negative, a1 grammar, common esl mistakes, im not, beginner english
